newsitem.title: UKRAINE: More shares to buy in Ukraine shipbuilder.
newsitem.headline: More shares to buy in Ukraine shipbuilder.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund will increase the number of shares available to foreign investors in the privatisation of the Mykolayiv shipbuilder Okean, the company's general director said on Monday.
"The Fund has accepted a resolution to enlarge the number of shares available to foreign investors from 16 to 36 percent," Mykola Romanchuk told Reuters.

Okean, the only one of three shipbuilders in the Black Sea port city of Mykolayiv to undergo privatisation, is on a list of 208 state enterprises made available for strategic foreign or domestic investment by the Fund, the state privatisation agency.
Privatisation will take place next year, Romanchuk said.

State shares will be reduced to 24 from 30 percent, shares owned by the enterprise's 7,000 workers will grow to 30.9 from 20 percent, and 9.1 percent of shares will be sold to the public through privatisation certificate auctions, he said.
Okean's starting capital is valued at 3.85 million hryvnia ($2.1 million).

Romanchuk said Okean, built in the 1970s and one of Ukraine's newest shipbuilders, is building two cargo container ships for a United Arab Emirates firm, and two 70,000-tonne carriers for Ukraine's Black Sea Shipping Company.
The company is also negotiating contracts with French and British companies.
Romanchuk said Okean's ships are constructed at a price 20 percent lower than world prices.
"This is what works for us best, and the lower cost is tied in with lower price of labour in Ukraine," he said.
